title: Foundations: Swing Vocal - The Complete Guide
summary: What Swing Vocal is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Swing Vocal songs: Swing vocals ride the big-band wave: brassy, rhythmic singing built for dance halls, with call-and-response horn sections and a four-on-the-floor pulse. Sinatra, Ella, and Nat King Cole defined cool.

History: The swing era (1935–1945) put singers in front of big bands: Benny Goodman, Count Basie, Duke Ellington. Frank Sinatra's 1940s bobby-soxer fame and 1950s Capitol records set the vocal standard.

How the songs work: Swing Vocal favors the keys of F, Bb, Eb, C. Common forms include Verse-chorus with big-band shout chorus; Ballad intro then double-time swing. Players should master phrasing behind the beat like a horn first, then the big finish: held high note over a band hit. Big-band keys; singers pick their best.

title: Fly Me to the Moon - Swing Vocal Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Fly Me to the Moon by Bart Howard / Sinatra-Basie (1964).
body:
Fly Me to the Moon — Bart Howard / Sinatra-Basie, 1964. The Apollo 11 astronauts played it on the moon.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of Eb):
D# | C7 | Fm7 | A#7

This study chart uses the 'Rhythm changes' progression, the Swing Vocal workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus with big-band shout chorus. Listen for scat breaks trading with the brass — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Swing Vocal pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let scat breaks trading with the brass. Big-band keys; singers pick their best. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
